body.h4: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: Around 4 in 10 adults (41%) who pay energy bills said it was very or somewhat difficult to afford them.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: This was according to those asked between 17 and 28 January 2024 as part of our latest [Public opinions and social trends bulletin](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/publicopinionsandsocialtrendsgreatbritain17to28january2024).

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: This proportion was at a high of 49% in the period covering 17 to 29 May 2023, but appears to have slowly decreased since then.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: The survey also revealed that 44% of adults in Great Britain are using less fuel, such as gas or electricity, in their homes because of the rising cost of living.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: Of the 49% of adults who reported that their cost of living had increased over the last month, 81% cited rising gas or electricity bills as a reason for this.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: Meanwhile, around one in five (19%) adults reported that they were occasionally, hardly ever, or never able to keep comfortably warm in their home in the past two weeks, according to [more detailed analysis of the survey, which covers the period 18 October, 2023 and 1 January, 2024](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/theimpactofwinterpressuresondifferentpopulationgroupsingreatbritain18october2023to1january2024).

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: This is a fall from nearly one in four adults (24%) during a similar period in 2022.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: In the year to January 2024 gas prices fell by 26.5% and electricity prices fell by 13.0%, according to the latest [Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers’ housing costs (CPIH)](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukjanuary2024) data.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: Inflation rates for gas and electricity have remained similar since October 2023, when the annual rate fell to its lowest level since records began in January 1989.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: Motor fuel prices continued to fall between December 2023 and January 2024.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: The average price of petrol fell by 2.9 pence per litre to 139.9 pence, while average diesel prices fell 3.1 pence per litre to 172.1 pence.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: Both are down on the prices seen in January 2023, when average petrol prices stood at 149.4 pence per litre, and diesel prices at 172.1 pence per litre.

body.h4: Around 4 in 10 energy bill payers struggling to afford payments
body.text: These meant overall motor fuel prices fell 9.2% in the year to January 2024, compared with a fall of 10.8% in the year to December 2023.
